facets.name: Undecided
facets.meaning: No decision has been made about this facet.

facets.name: Draft
facets.meaning: A proposed definition still being designed.

facets.name: In review
facets.meaning: A proposal being reviewed, not yet approved.

facets.name: Approved
facets.meaning: Approved design state; does not mean deployed or healthy.

facets.name: Deprecated
facets.meaning: Still identifiable but discouraged for future use.

facets.name: Retired
facets.meaning: Retired from intended use; retained history may still exist.

facets.name: Rejected
facets.meaning: A rejected design alternative, not an operational failure.

facets.name: Intended / target
facets.meaning: A design intention, distinct from observed deployment.

facets.name: Observed
facets.meaning: Observed fact with source and observation time.

facets.name: Inferred
facets.meaning: A derived hypothesis, not a confirmed fact.

facets.name: Verified
facets.meaning: Verified against explicitly named evidence and date.

facets.name: Synthetic example
facets.meaning: Generated illustrative values, not production observations.

facets.name: Sanitized example
facets.meaning: Transformed example data with its handling provenance recorded.

facets.name: Healthy
facets.meaning: Observed health within a stated window; not design approval.

facets.name: Degraded
facets.meaning: Observed degradation under a stated criterion.

facets.name: Failed
facets.meaning: An observed operational failure.

facets.name: Paused
facets.meaning: Execution or update propagation deliberately paused.

facets.name: Unknown health
facets.meaning: No reliable current operational health assertion.

facets.name: Transactional
facets.meaning: Operational transaction-oriented usage.

facets.name: Analytical
facets.meaning: Analytical usage; not automatically historical or read-only.

facets.name: Mixed workload
facets.meaning: Both transactional and analytical usage are explicitly intended.

facets.name: Streaming
facets.meaning: Continuous event-oriented processing or access.

facets.name: Batch
facets.meaning: Discrete scheduled or initiated processing.

facets.name: Interactive query
facets.meaning: Latency-sensitive user-driven querying.

facets.name: ML / feature usage
facets.meaning: A representation used in a defined model or feature workflow.

facets.name: Authoritative
facets.meaning: Authority for a stated subject or field scope.

facets.name: Derived
facets.meaning: Produced from other data under an explicit derivation.

facets.name: Replica role
facets.meaning: Maintained copy of a stated source or fragment.

facets.name: Cache role
facets.meaning: Replaceable representation with an explicit source of truth.

facets.name: Archive role
facets.meaning: Retained primarily for historical or preservation purposes.

facets.name: Externally supplied
facets.meaning: An external producer controls the supplied data contract.

facets.name: Read and write
facets.meaning: Declared mutation and reading capability, independent of authority.

facets.name: Read only
facets.meaning: Declared read-only interface or permission scope.

facets.name: Current-state only
facets.meaning: No historical query capability is asserted in this view.

facets.name: Valid / business time
facets.meaning: When a fact applies in the business domain.

facets.name: Recorded / system time
facets.meaning: When a named system recorded a version as current knowledge.

facets.name: Bitemporal
facets.meaning: Both valid and recorded axes; identify the source system for recorded time.

facets.name: Event time
facets.meaning: Time assigned to occurrence of the event, not arrival time.

facets.name: Ingestion time
facets.meaning: Time data arrived at a specified receiving system.

facets.name: Processing time
facets.meaning: Time of processing in a specified engine or activity.

facets.name: Snapshot support
facets.meaning: Captured version or state with explicit consistency scope.

facets.name: Event history
facets.meaning: Retained event history; does not by itself guarantee reconstructability.

facets.name: Point-in-time recovery
facets.meaning: Recovery capability with a restore window, not a query-time axis.

facets.name: Expiry / retention
facets.meaning: Named expiry or retention policy with exceptions.

facets.name: Immutable / append-only
facets.meaning: Mutation restrictions with their exact scope stated.

facets.name: Local / on-premises
facets.meaning: A declared local placement; no security guarantee implied.

facets.name: Cloud hosted
facets.meaning: A declared cloud placement; not an assertion of managed operation.

facets.name: Edge deployed
facets.meaning: A device-side or near-source deployment.

facets.name: Hybrid composition
facets.meaning: A composite spans placement categories; bind each instance separately.

facets.name: Provider managed
facets.meaning: A provider operates the stated service scope.

facets.name: Self managed
facets.meaning: The stated organization operates the service scope.

facets.name: Development environment
facets.meaning: A development instance, not a draft-design status.

facets.name: Test environment
facets.meaning: A test instance and its isolation expectations.

facets.name: Staging environment
facets.meaning: A pre-production instance with declared purpose.

facets.name: Production environment
facets.meaning: A production instance; not automatically approved or healthy.

facets.name: Hash partitioning
facets.meaning: Partition policy uses a declared hash key and mapping.

facets.name: Range partitioning
facets.meaning: Partition policy uses explicit range boundaries.

facets.name: List partitioning
facets.meaning: Partition membership is assigned by explicit values.

facets.name: Composite partitioning
facets.meaning: More than one named partitioning level or method.

facets.name: Sharded
facets.meaning: Logical data is distributed as fragments; expose placements separately.

facets.name: Replicated
facets.meaning: Copies are maintained under a named replication policy.

facets.name: Primary / leader
facets.meaning: A current role within a named replication or coordination scope.

facets.name: Follower
facets.meaning: A following-copy role with freshness and write policy declared.

facets.name: Multi-writer
facets.meaning: Multiple writers with an explicit conflict and convergence policy.

facets.name: Co-located
facets.meaning: A stated distribution or placement alignment requirement.

facets.name: Replication factor parameter
facets.meaning: A numeric policy value; expand which copy classes count.

facets.name: Quorum parameter
facets.meaning: A stated quorum rule and membership scope, not a universal consistency promise.

facets.name: Public
facets.meaning: Public under a named classification policy.

facets.name: Internal
facets.meaning: Internal-use classification under a named policy.

facets.name: Confidential
facets.meaning: Confidential classification; include handling rules.

facets.name: Restricted
facets.meaning: Restricted classification; include approved access policy.

facets.name: Personal information
facets.meaning: Personal-data classification with jurisdiction and scope specified.

facets.name: Encrypted
facets.meaning: Encryption in a stated location or transfer scope, with key policy.

facets.name: Masked / tokenized
facets.meaning: A specific field transformation; identify reversibility and authority.

facets.name: Row-level access
facets.meaning: A row-scoped access policy, not an arbitrary box colour.

facets.name: Column-level access
facets.meaning: A column-scoped access policy.

facets.name: Residency requirement
facets.meaning: A required allowed-location set, distinct from observed placement.

facets.name: Legal hold
facets.meaning: A scoped preservation exception overriding ordinary deletion where applicable.

facets.name: Primary key member
facets.meaning: Membership in an identified primary key; list composite grouping.

facets.name: Alternate / unique key
facets.meaning: Membership in an identified alternate key, not generic mandatory-ness.

facets.name: Reference / foreign key member
facets.meaning: Field-level reference; enforcement is an independent property.

facets.name: Partition / distribution key
facets.meaning: Member of the declared distribution key, with order if applicable.

facets.name: Clustering / ordering key
facets.meaning: Member of a named clustering or ordering definition.

facets.name: Required presence
facets.meaning: A property must exist; this alone says nothing about null.

facets.name: Optional presence
facets.meaning: A property may be absent; this alone says nothing about null.

facets.name: Nullable value
facets.meaning: The value may be null; not equivalent to missing.

facets.name: Non-null value
facets.meaning: Null is disallowed; state presence separately where applicable.

facets.name: Generated / computed
facets.meaning: A computed, defaulted or generated value with expression metadata.

facets.name: Embedded structure
facets.meaning: A nested value; use explicit embedding relations when expanded.

facets.name: Repeated value
facets.meaning: A repeated value with ordering and cardinality constraints.

facets.name: Semantic domain binding
facets.meaning: Field uses an approved semantic domain.

facets.name: Candidate domain binding
facets.meaning: Suggested shared domain pending review.

facets.name: Ascending order
facets.meaning: Ascending order within a specifically named key or list.

facets.name: Descending order
facets.meaning: Descending order within a specifically named key or list.

facets.name: Change capture
facets.meaning: Capture method; not a transport or an end-to-end guarantee.

facets.name: Snapshot transfer
facets.meaning: A transfer of captured state with consistency scope.

facets.name: Extract-transform-load
facets.meaning: Transformation before loading to the named destination.

facets.name: Extract-load-transform
facets.meaning: Load before the named target-side transformation.

facets.name: Publish / broadcast
facets.meaning: Publish to a named channel; define consumer semantics separately.

facets.name: Polling
facets.meaning: Periodic read-based collection with cursor or watermark policy.

facets.name: API transport
facets.meaning: Transfer over a specified API interaction.

facets.name: File transfer
facets.meaning: Transfer using specified file artifacts and atomicity rules.

facets.name: Kafka transport
facets.meaning: Technology tag only; delivery guarantees must be separately specified.

facets.name: Batch movement
facets.meaning: A bounded set or scheduled transfer.

facets.name: Continuous movement
facets.meaning: An ongoing stream or repeated incremental propagation.

facets.name: At-most-once requirement
facets.meaning: A scoped delivery requirement; distinguish intended from verified.

facets.name: At-least-once requirement
facets.meaning: Duplicates are possible; define sink and consumer handling.

facets.name: Exactly-once effect claim
facets.meaning: Requires a stated end-to-end scope and supporting evidence.

facets.name: Ordering scope
facets.meaning: Ordering by key, partition or global scope explicitly stated.

facets.name: Idempotent application
facets.meaning: Repeated application has a stated equivalent effect under defined inputs.

facets.name: Dead-letter routing
facets.meaning: Rejected messages route to an explicit destination and recovery process.

facets.name: Retry policy
facets.meaning: A declared retry, backoff and exhaustion policy.

facets.name: Undecided value
facets.meaning: A required design choice has not been decided.

facets.name: Not applicable
facets.meaning: The property does not apply to this element.

facets.name: Known but hidden
facets.meaning: Presentation hides a value; semantic metadata remains intact.

facets.name: Absent / not supplied
facets.meaning: No assertion was supplied; do not infer undecided or false.

facets.name: Conflicting evidence
facets.meaning: Incompatible assertions require reconciliation.

facets.name: More facets collapsed
facets.meaning: A count of omitted badges, with expansion or a details link.

endpoints: No direction or multiplicity is asserted.
Direction of dependency, mapping, control or governance; read the verb.
Forward payload movement or forward derivation; line pattern disambiguates.
Generalization: points toward the more general type.
Embedding: at the containing end, not at the child end.
Two bars: minimum one and maximum one.
Circle plus bar: optional single participation.
Bar plus crow foot: mandatory plural participation.
Circle plus crow foot: optional plural participation.
Numeric min..max replaces ambiguous or nonstandard multiplicity marks.
Attach to an identified interaction point or field, not arbitrary geometry.
A filled routing junction; crossing lines without a dot are not joined.
design_state_rule: No facet writes design.state or the status icon.
